headline: MicroG GmsCore offers free Android Play Services replacement
summary: This open-source project allows apps to run on AOSP-based ROMs without proprietary Google Play Services, enhancing privacy and freedom.
details: MicroG GmsCore is a free software reimplementation of Google's Play Services. It enables applications that rely on proprietary Google APIs to function on Android Open Source Project (AOSP)-based ROMs, such as LineageOS, serving as an alternative to the non-free Google Play Services.

This project is a powerful tool for users seeking to enhance their privacy and freedom on Android devices. While apps using MicroG may still employ proprietary libraries to communicate, they do so through MicroG instead of direct communication with Google's services.

For GmsCore to operate correctly, the Android system must support signature spoofing, allowing GmsCore to mimic the presence of official Play Services to requesting applications. Specific ROMs offer out-of-the-box support, with other solutions available for those that do not.

The GmsCore package includes the Unified Network Location Provider module (UnifiedNlp), which manages application requests to Google's network location provider. A full MicroG setup also requires installing a replacement for the Play Store, such as MicroG Companion.

The project's implementation status for various APIs is detailed on its wiki. Users are encouraged to report bugs with comprehensive information, including logs, screenshots, version numbers, and device details. For sensitive data in logs, private messaging is an option.
